scope: H0/H1 native render-to-texture publication through the bounded persistent AXI host; one previously hot texture line, acknowledged exports, binding reinterpretation and VM rebinding. H4 cluster/throughput and full H0-H8 closure remain open.

profiles.backend: actual shared shader CUs, FPU enabled
actual shared shader CUs, FPU enabled

l2.selection: MobileGpuConfig().execution, with lane/warp overrides for reference profiles

functional.memory: 256-bit AXI; 8-cycle read delays, 17-cycle write acknowledgements. Track every W-export byte through B acknowledgement, including staging writes. Bare and Sv32 superpage mapping to +4 MiB; unchanged VA for the texture across jobs.
functional.workload: One 8x8, 1x tile within a 16x16 viewport. Two ordered overlapping triangle records per job; the first wins LESS. Each job exports a 32-bit color plane and D24S8 plane at 512-byte row pitch.
functional.shader: Real RV32 vector passthrough for the producer and vtex.sample for sampling jobs; capacity-based SoA offsets, configured vector length and two staging banks per worker.
functional.checks_per_job: 64 color words and 64 depth/stencil words checked against independent expected values, including uncovered clear pixels. Unified command ID, success status, 320 command bytes and all 512 exported attachment bytes acknowledged before retirement.
functional.test_counting: Three new system checks. Each runs both VM modes and five jobs per mode. The negative-control failure and earlier fixture-debug runs are not passing checks. Earlier 56-check descriptor/host evidence is separate; no repeat of that cohort is claimed.

sequence.action: Sample the initial image at one interior texel; uniform white fixed-function input or direct vtex.sample shader output.
Repeat sampling with identical binding; assert texture word requests occur but the source line stays hot.
Render a different color into the source image. Queue a consumer with distinct immutable descriptor/command allocations during the first producer descriptor read.
Its first descriptor fetch must observe the producer success result, all 512 attachment bytes acknowledged, no pending B replies and the exact producer image. Then sample the new image.
Interpret the same bytes/VA as BGRA and export to an RGBA view. Assert fresh channel/alpha decoding and raw L2 reuse.

oracles.fixed_modulation: Each RGB channel is floor(255*texel_channel/256); alpha is opaque. Shared shaders export the sampled packed RGBA word including alpha.
oracles.scope: Source-line fetch counts exclude instruction, staging, page-table, descriptor and other memory traffic. They are cache-visibility checks, not frame bandwidth or throughput measurements.

negative_control.mutation: Temporarily add && false.B to the resident-hit invalidation condition in SharedL2Cache storeAllocate. No production mutation retained.

expected_failure.meaning: Old sampled RGB was reused despite the producer rendering new contents.

negative_control.restoration: Original L2 source restored byte-for-byte in the wrapper finally block; final all-profile positive run recompiles and uses that restored source.

limitations: Only the existing one-image binding and 1x1 sampler view of an 8x8 rendered image are exercised; general image bounds, layers/mips, texture formats, filtering and cluster throughput are not qualified.
Current persistent profile has one resident tile and serializes dependent jobs/memory engines. Region-scoped dependencies and concurrent independent engines remain required.
128 KiB L2 and the proposed four-CU/16-lane/eight-warp configuration are validated functionally with SRAM models. No new physical, clock, area, energy, sustained-scaling or frame-rate claim follows.
No CPU-cache coherence or synchronization of unrelated shader side effects is implied.
Mixed in-pass clear/draw host commands, general bounded resources, two tile engines, product driver/API adoption and all remaining H0-H8 gates remain open.
